night.does: Magnesium helps muscles relax and supports normal nerve function and a calmer evening wind-down.
night.form: Glycinate is magnesium bound to the amino acid glycine. It is gentle on the stomach and absorbs well, unlike magnesium oxide.
night.look: The elemental magnesium amount. The 1000 mg is the glycinate compound, not pure magnesium.
night.ev: Strong for magnesium status; moderate for sleep quality.
night.caution: People with kidney disease should check with a doctor first.

night.does: A traditional adaptogen herb. Studies on KSM-66 root extract show lower perceived stress and better sleep quality in adults.
night.form: KSM-66 is a full-spectrum root extract with published human trials, not leaf or generic powder.
night.look: The extract name, the plant part (root) and the withanolide percentage.
night.caution: Avoid in pregnancy and breastfeeding. Check with a doctor if you have thyroid or autoimmune conditions or take sedatives.

night.does: Supports normal immune function, protein synthesis and recovery. Zinc also contributes to the maintenance of normal testosterone levels.
night.form: Picolinate is a well-absorbed chelated form.
night.ev: Strong for zinc status and immunity.
night.caution: Long-term high intake can lower copper. Taking it on an empty stomach can cause nausea.

night.does: The body's own sleep-timing hormone. Helps with falling asleep, jet lag and shifted sleep schedules.
night.form: 3 mg is a widely used dose. More is not better.
night.look: Exact mg per tablet and whether it is immediate or extended release.
night.ev: Strong for sleep timing and jet lag; modest for general insomnia.
night.caution: Can cause drowsiness. Do not drive after taking it. Not for children, pregnancy or breastfeeding without medical advice.

day.time: Morning, with a meal that has some fat
day.does: Vitamin D3 supports bone, muscle and immune function, and vitamin K2 works alongside it for normal bone health. Low levels of D are common, so a blood test is the best way to know your need.
day.form: D3 (cholecalciferol) raises blood levels more reliably than D2, and K2 is paired with it for bone support.
day.look: D3 in IU and mcg (4000 IU equals 100 mcg) and the K2 amount in mcg.
day.ev: Strong for D3 where blood levels are low; moderate for K2 and bone health.
day.caution: 4000 IU is the commonly cited adult upper limit, so do not stack other vitamin D products without a blood test. Vitamin K can interfere with warfarin-type blood thinners, so check with a doctor first.

day.does: A traditional resin rich in fulvic acid. Small trials suggest support for energy and male vitality.
day.form: Purified shilajit, tested for heavy metals, is the only kind we consider.
day.look: Purification method, fulvic acid percentage and a third-party heavy metal report.
day.caution: Raw, unpurified shilajit can carry heavy metals. Avoid with iron overload conditions unless a doctor approves.

day.does: EPA and DHA support heart, brain and joint health.
day.form: Softgel fish oil in triglyceride form absorbs better with food.
day.look: EPA and DHA in mg separately, not just "1000 mg fish oil". Also look for third-party purity testing.
day.ev: Strong for triglycerides and heart health; mixed for mood and focus.
day.caution: Check with a doctor if you take blood thinners or have a fish or shellfish allergy.

day.does: Supports energy-yielding metabolism, red blood cells and normal nerve function.
day.form: Methylcobalamin is the active form; cyanocobalamin is the cheaper, stable one. The final form will be stated on the label.
day.look: The form and the dose in mcg.
day.ev: Strong if you are low (vegetarians and vegans especially); little effect if you are not.
day.caution: Metformin and some acid reducers lower B12 levels.
